archetype.name: Underachiever (lineup collapse)
archetype.definition: Toronto came off a 94-win season with 10 playoff wins and the site's No. 1 ranking, then fell to 79-83 and last in the AL East when its offense dropped from fourth in runs to dead last, leaving an elite bullpen and defense with too little to protect.

report.headline: An A+ bullpen couldn't rescue the league's lowest-scoring lineup

recap.finish: 79-83, fifth in the AL East (19 games behind Tampa Bay); missed the postseason
recap.body:
This was a run-prevention team with no offense. Toronto finished 10th in runs allowed per game, ninth in team ERA at 3.90, second in Fielding Runs and with an A+ bullpen. It also finished 30th of 30 in runs scored and 28th in OPS at .691, in a park that plays slightly in hitters' favor at 102. The lineup scored 648 runs and allowed 694. That 46-run deficit works out to the -0.28 Run Diff per game, 21st in the league, and it marks a team that was modestly worse than average, not a disaster.

The season never built momentum. After a 4-1 March, April went 10-16, and the club was outscored 120-96. May at 15-14 was the only stretch of the first half with a positive margin. June (11-15, outscored 129-101) and July (11-13) left the Jays at 51-59 heading into August. A 17-11 August got them to 68-70 and briefly back in sight of .500, but a 11-13 September ended it. The best winning streak all year was four games. A team that never strings together five straight wins does not climb out of a hole. The final ten went 4-6, including three straight one- and two-run losses in Baltimore, and the Orioles finished a half game ahead of Toronto for fourth.

The offense is the story. Kazuma Okamoto carried it with 33 homers and a 113 wRC+. Alejandro Kirk hit at a 114 wRC+ but played only 79 games. Springer and Lukes were a bit above average. Everything else sagged. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. slugged .356 with 9 homers and a 95 wRC+ in 609 PA, which is far too little power from a first baseman. Ernie Clement (.285 OBP, 80 wRC+), Andrés Giménez (81) and Myles Straw (83) all took heavy playing time below average. Giménez at least earned his 2.8 WAR with 14.1 Def Runs at short. The hitters graded D-, and the run total backs it up.

The pitching split in two. Dylan Cease was an ace: 2.40 ERA, 239 strikeouts, 5.5 WAR, sixth on the starters' tab. Louis Varland was nearly unhittable closing games, with a 1.27 ERA and 35 saves. Tyler Rogers (1.77 ERA, 33 holds) and Spencer Miles (2.73 over 95.2 innings) made the bullpen the league's best group. The rotation still graded only a D because the back end gave away a lot. Michael Lorenzen threw 127.1 innings at a 7.21 ERA and ranked 207th of 215 starters. Spencer Arrighetti posted a 5.44 FIP with a 13% walk rate.

The record actually flattered the team. W vs Run Diff was +3.1, so the differential alone points to roughly a 76-win club. Last year's 94 wins also came with a +5.5 cushion. The 2024 team (74-88, 23rd in runs, .702 OPS) looks a lot like this one. The 2025 offense, fourth in runs, is the outlier in recent history, not this year's.

highlights.title: A bullpen that closed every door
highlights.body: The relief corps graded A+. Varland ranked fourth of 389 relievers with a 1.27 ERA and a 1.83 FIP, so his dominance was earned and not lucky. Rogers and Fluharty combined for 53 holds in front of him. Some of it will regress: Rogers' 1.77 ERA sat on a 3.35 FIP, and Braydon Fisher's 3.21 ERA hid a 4.38 FIP and a 14.2% walk rate.

highlights.title: Cease pitched like an ace
highlights.body: Cease's 2.40 ERA was backed by a 2.56 FIP and a 34.9% strikeout rate. That is genuine dominance, and his 5.5 WAR led the roster. His 11.4% walk rate is the one thing keeping him from being even better.

highlights.title: Elite team defense
highlights.body: Toronto saved 29.3 runs in the field, second in the league, a level it has also reached in recent seasons. Giménez (14.1 Def Runs) and Lukes (9.5) led the way. The defense is a big reason the run prevention ranked 10th with a rotation that graded D.

lowlights.title: Last in the league in runs
lowlights.body: The offense fell from fourth in runs in 2025 to 30th, with a .691 OPS in a slightly hitter-friendly park. Only Okamoto supplied real power. Guerrero's .356 slugging at first base was the biggest single hole, and Clement, Giménez and Straw all logged heavy playing time with a wRC+ in the low 80s.

lowlights.title: Rotation's back end gave games away
lowlights.body: Behind Cease, Soriano and Yesavage were serviceable. Lorenzen's 7.21 ERA over 127.1 innings was among the league's worst, and his 5.45 FIP says it wasn't bad luck. Arrighetti's 5.44 FIP with a 13% walk rate was little better. Together they explain the rotation's D grade.

lowlights.title: No streak to climb out
lowlights.body: The longest winning streak was four games. Losing months in April and June left the club eight games under .500 by the end of July. The 17-11 August was the only real push, and it couldn't overcome the summer deficit.

arc.note: The team hovered below .500 all year: a bad April, a level May, a slide through June and July to 51-59, an August surge to 68-70, and a losing September.

recap.nextYear: The pieces that worked are concentrated in a few players. Cease and Varland were among the best at their roles, Okamoto was the only consistent power source, and Kirk hit well in half a season. The bullpen and defense should stay strengths, though Rogers' and Fisher's ERAs ran well ahead of their FIPs, so expect the relief group to give back some runs. The hitters (D-) are the group that needs the most work, starting with Guerrero's lost power and the light bats at second, short and center. The rotation needs a real replacement for Lorenzen's innings. Also discount the 79 wins: a +3.1 W vs Run Diff means the underlying team was closer to 76 wins, and recent history (2024's 74 wins, 2025's 94 with a +5.5 cushion) suggests last year's offense, not this one, was the exception.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; the run totals, grades and FIP checks all agree.
